title: e-Shram registration for unorganised and gig workers
text: e-Shram is the government's national database of unorganised workers, including gig and platform workers. Registration is free on the e-Shram portal or at a Common Service Centre. Usually needed: Aadhaar, a mobile number linked to Aadhaar, and a bank account. It is meant for workers aged 16 to 59 who are not EPFO or ESIC members and do not pay income tax. You get an e-Shram card with a Universal Account Number. Helpline: 14434.

title: PM Shram Yogi Maan-dhan (PM-SYM) pension
text: PM-SYM is a voluntary pension scheme for unorganised workers aged 18 to 40 with monthly income up to Rs 15,000 who are not in EPFO, ESIC or NPS. After age 60 the worker gets an assured minimum pension of Rs 3,000 per month. The worker pays a small monthly amount based on age and the Central Government pays an equal amount. Enrol at a Common Service Centre with Aadhaar and a bank account.

title: Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY health cover
text: Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY gives health cover of up to Rs 5 lakh per family per year for treatment in listed hospitals. Eligibility is decided from government records, so you cannot simply apply. Check if you are eligible on the PM-JAY website or call 14555. Take your Aadhaar or ration card to the Ayushman Mitra desk at a listed hospital.

title: Code on Social Security, 2020 and gig workers
text: The Code on Social Security, 2020 formally recognises gig workers and platform workers. It provides for social security schemes for them, partly funded by contributions from aggregators (platform companies). The benefits you actually get depend on the schemes notified by the central or state government, so confirm with your state Labour Department.

title: Where to complain about unpaid money or unfair treatment at work
text: First raise the issue in the platform's in-app support or grievance option and ask for a written reason. Keep screenshots, trip or order IDs, payment records and messages as proof. If it is not solved, you can complain to the Labour Commissioner or Labour Department office of your state, especially for unpaid wages or unfair treatment. Your state Labour Department website lists the office near you.

title: Emergency numbers
text: In an emergency dial 112 from any phone for police, fire or ambulance. Ambulance service is 108 in most states. Women in distress can call 1091 or 181 in many states.

title: Road safety for riders and drivers
text: Wear a good helmet on a two-wheeler; it is required by law. Do not use the phone while riding or driving; stop safely first. Keep to speed limits even when an order timer is running. Carry your licence, RC and insurance papers. Check brakes, tyres and lights before long shifts.

title: Working safely in hot weather
text: In very hot weather drink water often even if you are not thirsty, take short breaks in the shade, wear light cotton clothes and cover your head. Avoid long work in the peak afternoon heat when you can. Dizziness, headache, vomiting or confusion can be heatstroke: move to shade, cool the body with water and call 108 or go to a hospital.

title: Safety during night shifts
text: On night shifts share your live location with a family member, prefer well-lit routes, keep your phone charged and keep emergency numbers saved. If you feel unsafe at a pick-up or drop, you can cancel, report it to platform support and, if needed, call 112.

title: Online payment fraud
text: If you lose money to online fraud or a fake payment link, call 1930 quickly and report at cybercrime.gov.in. Never share your OTP, UPI PIN or card details with anyone, even if they say they are from the platform or the bank.

title: Driving licence through Parivahan Sarathi
text: Apply for or renew a driving licence on the Parivahan Sarathi portal. You usually need age proof, address proof and passport photos, and a learner's licence comes first. Book a driving test slot online and pay the fee there. Check the portal for the licence type needed to carry passengers for hire.

title: Jan Dhan bank account
text: A Jan Dhan account is a basic bank account that can be opened with zero balance at any bank branch. Aadhaar is the usual ID. Linking the account with Aadhaar and your mobile number helps government benefits reach you directly.

title: Central measures for gig and platform workers
text: The Code on Social Security, 2020 came into force on 21 November 2025. It defines gig and platform workers and allows schemes for them such as life and disability cover, accident insurance, and health and maternity benefits. Platforms (aggregators) must pay 1 to 2 percent of their annual turnover, capped at 5 percent of what they pay such workers, into a Social Security Fund. Platform workers can register on the e-Shram portal, which has a separate module for platforms. The Union Budget 2025-26 announced identity cards, e-Shram registration and health cover under PM-JAY for platform workers. Which benefits you actually get depends on the schemes notified, so confirm on e-Shram or with your Labour Department.

title: Which states have dedicated gig worker laws
text: Reports in 2026 list dedicated state laws for platform gig workers in Rajasthan (2023), Karnataka (2025), Jharkhand (2025), Bihar (2025) and Telangana (2026). Each state has its own rules, board and fees, and implementation differs. Select your city or tell me your state to see the rules that apply to you. If your state is not listed, ask your state Labour Department what is available now.

title: Rajasthan gig workers law
text: The Rajasthan Platform Based Gig Workers (Registration and Welfare) Act, 2023 was the first such state law. A Welfare Board registers gig workers, aggregators and primary employers, and notifies social security schemes. A Social Security and Welfare Fund is built from a welfare fee on platform transactions. Registered workers who face violations of their rights, payments or benefits can file a petition with the competent authority named by the state government. Check with the Rajasthan Labour Department what is working now.

title: Karnataka gig workers law
text: Karnataka's Platform-Based Gig Workers (Social Security and Welfare) Act, 2025 requires platforms operating in Karnataka to register under the Act, and eligible gig workers can register to get welfare schemes. It creates a welfare fund, and platforms pay a welfare fee on transactions involving gig workers. The law is contested, so check its current status with the Karnataka Labour Department.

title: Bihar gig workers law
text: Bihar passed a gig workers welfare law in 2025. It provides for registration of gig workers, a welfare board and social security benefits; reports mention provident fund, maternity benefits and old-age protection. News reports said progress in Bihar had stalled, so check with the Bihar Labour Department what is available now.

title: Jharkhand gig workers law
text: Jharkhand passed its gig workers welfare law in 2025. It offers registration and an ID for gig workers and links the welfare board to the state Labour Department's portal. Reports said Jharkhand was further along in implementation than other states; confirm the current status with the Jharkhand Labour Department.

title: Telangana gig workers law
text: The Telangana Assembly passed the Telangana Platform-Based Gig Workers (Registration, Social Security and Welfare) law in 2026. It sets up a welfare board to register gig workers, a welfare fund financed by a 1 to 2 percent levy on platform transactions, and a grievance system. Platforms with at least 100 workers must have an internal dispute committee, and there are district-level complaint mechanisms for sudden termination or stopped payments. Check with the Telangana Labour Department whether it is in force.

title: Tamil Nadu gig workers welfare board
text: Tamil Nadu set up the Tamil Nadu Platform Based Gig Workers' Welfare Board in December 2023 under the Tamil Nadu Manual Workers (Regulation of Employment and Conditions of Work) Act, 1982. Registration was started through the state Labour department's existing welfare boards. An early news report found very few gig workers enrolled, so ask the Tamil Nadu Labour Department how to register now.

title: Maharashtra gig workers bill (2026)
text: The Maharashtra government introduced the Maharashtra Gig and Platform Workers Rights and Protection Bill, 2026 on 3 July 2026. It proposes registration of gig workers, welfare measures, a welfare board, duties for platforms, and a grievance process. A bill is not a law until it is passed and comes into force, so check with the Maharashtra Labour Department whether that has happened.
